L’ACCENT On retrouve ici la règle bien connue qui est d’application dans la plupart des parlers maghrébins étudiés jusqu’ici, à savoir que dans un mot polysyllabique l’accent tombe sur la syllabe finale si elle est doublement fermée (CvC, CvCC), tandis qu’il tombe sur la pénultième si la syllabe finale est ouverte ou simplement fermée (Cv, Cv, CvC, Cv). En termes plus phonologiques, on pourra dire aussi que l’accent «se place sur la troisième more du mot — ou sur la quatrième si la troisième est constituée par une consonne» (1). a. new_statements.translation: D. ACCENT. We find here the well-known rule that applies in most of the Maghrebi dialects studied so far, namely that in a polysyllabic word the accent falls on the final syllable if it is doubly closed (Cv̄C, CvCC), whereas it falls on the penultimate if the final syllable is open or simply closed (Cv, Cv̄, CvC, Cv̆). In more phonological terms one may also say that the accent 'is placed on the third mora of the word — or on the fourth if the third is constituted by a consonant'. a. Accent on the final syllable: sâbʕîn 'seventy', ḥârâbt 'I made war'. b. Accent on the penult: titḥaḍḍar 'you will get ready', âḫŏr 'last'.

new_statements.translation_language: French (archive.org OCR; vowel-length diacritics on the syllable templates and some transcription characters lost: '(CvC, CvCC)' = (Cv̄C, CvCC); '(Cv, Cv, CvC, Cv)' = (Cv, Cv̄, CvC, Cv̆) or similar; sâhdn = sâbʕîn, îthàdddr = titḥaḍḍar, âhdr = âḫŏr)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Maghrebi weight rule: stress the final syllable when it is superheavy (long vowel + C, or short vowel + CC); otherwise stress the penult. Equivalently, stress the syllable containing the third mora counted from the end of the word (fourth if the third mora is a coda consonant). Ultra-short (disjunctive) vowels never carry the accent.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing on secondary stress in the retrievable text.
new_statements.exceptions: Grand'Henry notes 'l'instabilité de l'accent dans les formes impératives' (accent unstable in imperatives, tied to old short vowels) and that ultra-short vowels 'ne portent jamais l'accent'. Dhina 1938 (same dialect type, Laghouat 'Arbâʕ) adds form-specific facts distinguishing these Saharan dialects from Tell dialects: accent stays on the first syllable in bägᵉrti 'ma vache', ḫášᵉbtu, mäṭᵉḥnä, mukᵉḥlä (pp. 334-335) and on the first radical vowel in sémʕätu, ḍárǝbtek 'elle l'a entendu / t'a frappé' (p. 321), where Tell dialects shift/geminate.
new_statements.domain_note: Word domain ('dans un mot polysyllabique'); examples are citation forms including inflected verb forms. The variety is the Arabic of nomadic, semi-nomadic and recently sedentarised Arab groups of the Mzab region (Berriane, Ghardaïa Chaanba and Mdâbîḥ, Metlili, Sebseb, Hassi Fhal, with Timimoun data), i.e. Cantineau's Saharan 'dialecte A'.
new_statements.identity_note: Grand'Henry 1976 describes the Arabic of the Arab (non-Mozabite) nomadic, semi-nomadic and sedentarised groups of the Mzab region — Berriane, Ghardaïa (Chaanba, Mdâbîḥ), Metlili, Sebseb, Hassi Fhal, plus Timimoun — i.e. Cantineau's Saharan 'dialecte A'; it is the grammar Glottolog attaches to alge1240 itself, so identity is exact. Dhina 1938 ('Arbâʕ = Larbaa confederation of Laghouat, close to the Ouled Naïl) is also Glottolog-listed under alge1240. Ph. Marçais 1945 (Bou-Saâda) and Slimani 2016-2018 (Djelfa, Ouled Naïl) describe dialects their authors place in the same type-A Saharan nomad group, but Bou-Saâda/Djelfa lie north of the Saharan Atlas and Glottolog/Ethnologue geography may file them under alge1239 (Algerian Arabic); treat them as supporting, not defining, evidence. Gębski 2024 (Jewish Wad-Souf) is a sedentary E-type (South-Tunisian-like) variety within the aao area.

sources.note: TOC: 'C. La syllabe 35 / D. L'accent 37'. p.37: the well-known Maghrebi rule applies: in a polysyllable the accent falls on the final syllable if it is 'doublement fermée' (Cv̄C, CvCC), otherwise (final open or simply closed) on the penult; = 'third mora of the word, or fourth if the third is a consonant'. Examples sâbʕîn, ḥârâbt (final) vs titḥaḍḍar, âḫŏr (penult). Elsewhere: ultra-short vowels never bear the accent; accent is unstable in imperative forms.

sources.note: No general accent rule; form-specific remarks only (verified on page images): p.321 3fs perfect + vowel-initial suffix has '1re voyelle radicale accentuée' (sémʕätu, ḍárǝbtek vs Tell semʕātu); p.333 faʕʕāliya adjectives with accented medium -a-; ʕámya 'avec accent sur 1re voy.'; p.334 mafʕala nouns (mäṭᵉḥnä, mukᵉḥlä) 'L'accent est également sur la 1re syllabe du mot, à l'état absolu'; p.335 faʕlat/faʕalat nouns + vowel-initial suffix (bägᵉrti, ḫášᵉbtu, no Tell-type gemination) 'L'accent frappe toujours la première syllabe'; p.324 imperative kûl with 'accentuation très marquée de la voyelle'.
